The low individual degree chapters use the same term for the concrete data of a two-prover strategy for the $(m,q,d)$ low individual degree test (Definition~\\ref{def:projective-strategy} in Chapter~\\ref{chap:test}); that definition is the specialization of the present notion to the question format of that particular test. The two usages occur in disjoint contexts.\n    98\t\\end{remark}\n    99\t\n   100\t\\begin{definition}[Symmetric games and symmetric strategies]\\label{def:symmetric-game}\n   101\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricGame, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricGame.toGame, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy}\n   102\t\t\\leanok\n   103\t\t% Paper label: rem:symmetric-games (a definition environment carrying a rem: label in the\n   104\t\t% source); relabeled here to match the environment kind.\n   105\t\t\\uses{def:game, def:tensor-product-strategy}\n   106\t\tA game $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal Y, \\mathcal A, \\mathcal B, \\mu, D)$ is \\emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both players (i.e.\\ $\\mathcal X = \\mathcal Y$ and $\\mathcal A = \\mathcal B$), the distribution $\\mu$ is symmetric (i.e.\\ $\\mu(x,y) = \\mu(y,x)$ for all $x,y$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players symmetrically (i.e.\\ $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$ for all $x,y,a,b$).\n   107\t\n   108\t\tA strategy $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, A, B)$ is \\emph{symmetric} if $\\ket{\\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\\mathcal H \\ot \\mathcal H$, for some Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors, and the measurement operators of both players are identical.\n   109\t\\end{definition}\n   110\t\n   111\tWe often specify symmetric games $\\mathfrak G$ and symmetric strategies $\\mathcal S$ using a compact notation: we write $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal A, \\mu, D)$ and $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, M)$, where $M$ denotes the set of measurement operators shared by both players.\n   112\t\n   113\t% Source statement (references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-99) kept in\n   114\t% its original form. The proof below records the approximate form the source argument\n   115\t% establishes and leaves the final attainment step unproved; see rem:symmetric-strat-limit.\n   116\t\\begin{lemma}[Symmetrization of strategies for symmetric games]\\label{lem:symmetric-strat}\n   117\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_symmetric_projective_strategy}\n   118\t\t\\uses{def:symmetric-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:projective-strategy-general}\n   119\t\tLet $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal A, \\mu, D)$ be a symmetric game such that $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G) = 1-\\eps$ for some $\\eps \\ge 0$. Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, M)$ such that $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S) \\ge 1-\\eps$.\n   120\t\\end{lemma}\n   121\t\\begin{proof}\n   122\t\t\\uses{thm:naimark}\n   123\t\tThe symmetrization argument establishes the following approximate form of the conclusion: for every $\\eps' > \\eps$ there exists a symmetric and projective strategy of value at least $1-\\eps'$. Indeed, fix $\\eps' > \\eps$. Since $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G)$ is the supremum of the values of all strategies, there exists a strategy $\\mathcal S' = (\\ket{\\psi'}, A, B)$ with $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S') \\ge 1-\\eps'$. Using Naimark dilation (Theorem~\\ref{thm:naimark}), each dilated sub-measurement being completed to a projective measurement by assigning to one fixed outcome the residual projector of its family --- which changes no correlation on the extended state, as described in Remark~\\ref{rem:naimark-for-games} above --- we may assume without loss of generality that $\\ket{\\psi'} \\in \\C^d_{A'} \\ot \\C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ and that every $A^x$ and $B^x$ is a projective measurement. Let\n   124\t\t\\[\n   125\t\t\t\\ket{\\psi} = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt 2}\\, \\bigl( \\ket{0}_{A}\\ket{1}_{B}\\ket{\\psi'}_{A'B'} + \\ket{1}_{A}\\ket{0}_{B}\\ket{\\psi'_\\tau}_{A'B'} \\bigr) \\in \\bigl(\\C^2_{A} \\ot \\C^d_{A'}\\bigr) \\ot \\bigl(\\C^2_{B} \\ot \\C^d_{B'}\\bigr)\\,,\n   126\t\t\\]\n   127\t\twhere $\\ket{\\psi'_\\tau}$ is obtained from $\\ket{\\psi'}$ by permuting the two players' registers; then $\\ket{\\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of the register pairs $AA'$ and $BB'$. For each question $x \\in \\mathcal X$ define the projective measurement $M^x = \\{M^x_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ on $\\C^2 \\ot \\C^d$ by\n   128\t\t\\[\n   129\t\t\tM^x_a = \\ket{0}\\bra{0} \\ot A^x_a + \\ket{1}\\bra{1} \\ot B^x_a\\,,\n   130\t\t\\]\n   131\t\tand let each player measure $M$ on their pair of registers. Because the decision predicate $D$ of the symmetric game treats the two players symmetrically, the resulting symmetric projective strategy $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, M)$ satisfies $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S) = \\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S') \\ge 1-\\eps'$. Note that this construction preserves the value of the strategy it is applied to exactly.\n   132\t\n   133\t\tThe statement asserts more, namely a single symmetric projective strategy of value at least $1-\\eps$ itself. Passing from the family of strategies constructed above to one attaining the bound $1-\\eps$ is an attainment step which the argument does not supply: the supremum defining $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G)$ in Definition~\\ref{def:tensor-product-value} ranges over strategies of unbounded dimension and need not be attained. This step remains unproved; the obstruction, and the forms of the lemma that the argument does prove, are documented in \\cite{gap:qpbt_symmetrization-attainment}. See also Remark~\\ref{rem:symmetric-strat-limit}.\n   134\t\\end{proof}\n   135\t\n   136\t\\begin{remark}[Attainment in the symmetrization lemma]\\label{rem:symmetric-strat-limit}\n   137\t\tThe proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:symmetric-strat} yields, for each $\\eps' > \\eps$, a symmetric projective strategy of value at least $1-\\eps'$. The conclusion as stated, at $\\eps' = \\eps$, does not follow from this: the dilated dimension $d$ may grow as $\\eps' \\downarrow \\eps$, and the supremum defining $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G)$ in Definition~\\ref{def:tensor-product-value} need not be attained by any strategy. The symmetrization construction itself is value-preserving, so the conclusion does hold whenever the hypothesis supplies an actual strategy of value at least $1-\\eps$ rather than only the value of the game; every use of the lemma in the source proceeds from such a strategy, or from a strict lower bound on the value, and therefore consumes only what the proof establishes. The gap and the available repairs are documented in \\cite{gap:qpbt_symmetrization-attainment}.\n   138\t\\end{remark}\n   139\t\n   140\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\\ref{lem:symmetric-strat}]\n   141\t\t\\label{lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy}\n   142\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy}\n   143\t\t\\leanok\n   144\t\t\\uses{def:symmetric-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:projective-strategy-general}\n   145\t\tThis formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper; it is the value-preserving given-strategy form of Lemma~\\ref{lem:symmetric-strat} isolated in Remark~\\ref{rem:symmetric-strat-limit}, and it is what the symmetrization argument actually proves. Let $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal A, \\mu, D)$ be a symmetric game and let $\\mathcal S'$ be a strategy for $\\mathfrak G$ with $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S') \\ge 1-\\eps$. Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, M)$ with\n   146\t\t\\[\n   147\t\t\t\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S) = \\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G, \\mathcal S') \\ge 1-\\eps\\,.\n   148\t\t\\]\n   149\t\\end{lemma}\n   150\t\\begin{proof}\n   151\t\t\\leanok\n   152\t\t\\uses{thm:naimark}\n   153\t\tApply Naimark dilation (Theorem~\\ref{thm:naimark}) to $\\mathcal S'$, completing each dilated family at one fixed outcome as described in Remark~\\ref{rem:naimark-for-games}, and then form the permutation-invariant state $\\ket{\\psi}$ and the block-diagonal measurements $M^x$ of the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:symmetric-strat}. Both steps preserve the value of the strategy they are applied to, so $\\mathcal S$ has exactly the value of $\\mathcal S'$. No attainment step is involved, since the strategy $\\mathcal S'$ is given rather than extracted from the supremum defining $\\operatorname{val}^*(\\mathfrak G)$.\n   154\t\\end{proof}\n   155\t\n   156\t\\begin{definition}[Commuting strategies]\\label{def:comm-strategy}\n   157\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCommutingOn, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy.IsCommuting}\n   158\t\t\\leanok\n   159\t\t\\uses{def:game, def:tensor-product-strategy}\n   160\t\tLet $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal Y, \\mathcal A, \\mathcal B, \\mu, D)$ be a game, and let $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\\mathfrak G$ such that $\\mathcal H_A = \\mathcal H_B$. We say that $\\mathcal S$ is a \\emph{commuting strategy for $\\mathfrak G$} if for all question pairs $(x,y)$ in the support of $\\mu$ (i.e.\\ all $(x,y)$ with $\\mu(x,y) > 0$) we have\n   161\t\t\\[\n   162\t\t\t[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0 \\qquad \\text{for all } a \\in \\mathcal A,\\ b \\in \\mathcal B\\,,\n   163\t\t\\]\n   164\t\twhere $[A,B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.\n   165\t\\end{definition}\n   166\t\n   167\t\\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]\\label{def:consistent-measurement}\n   168\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn}\n   169\t\t\\leanok\n   170\t\t\\uses{def:povm-conventions}\n   171\t\tLet $\\mathcal A$ be a finite set, let $\\ket{\\psi} \\in \\mathcal H \\ot \\mathcal H$ be a state, and let $\\{M_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ be a projective measurement on $\\mathcal H$. We say that \\emph{$\\{M_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ is consistent on $\\ket{\\psi}$} if and only if\n   172\t\t\\[\n   173\t\t\t\\forall a \\in \\mathcal A\\,, \\qquad M_a \\ot \\Id_B\\, \\ket{\\psi} = \\Id_A \\ot M_a\\, \\ket{\\psi}\\,.\n   174\t\t\\]\n   175\t\tWhen the state $\\ket{\\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that $\\{M_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ is consistent.\n   176\t\\end{definition}\n   177\t\n   178\tThe terminology arises from the fact that when the measurement $\\{M_a\\}$ is performed on both registers of $\\ket{\\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is\n   179\t\\[\n   180\t\t\\sum_a \\bra{\\psi} M_a \\ot M_a \\ket{\\psi} = \\sum_a \\bra{\\psi} \\Id_A \\ot (M_a)^2 \\ket{\\psi} = \\sum_a \\bra{\\psi} \\Id_A \\ot M_a \\ket{\\psi} = 1\\,,\n   181\t\\]\n   182\twhere the first equality is by the definition of consistency, the second uses that $\\{M_a\\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\\sum_a M_a = \\Id$.\n   183\t\n   184\t\\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]\\label{def:consistent-strategy}\n   185\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentStrategyOn, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent}\n   186\t\t\\leanok\n   187\t\t\\uses{def:consistent-measurement, def:projective-strategy-general}\n   188\t\tLet $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state $\\ket{\\psi} \\in \\mathcal H \\ot \\mathcal H$, for some Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$, defined on question alphabets $\\mathcal X$ and $\\mathcal Y$ and answer alphabets $\\mathcal A$ and $\\mathcal B$, respectively. We say that $\\mathcal S$ is \\emph{consistent} if for all $x \\in \\mathcal X$ the measurement $\\{A^x_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ is consistent on $\\ket{\\psi}$, and for all $y \\in \\mathcal Y$ the measurement $\\{B^y_b\\}_{b \\in \\mathcal B}$ is consistent on $\\ket{\\psi}$.\n   189\t\\end{definition}\n   190\t\n   191\tWe almost always restrict attention to symmetric strategies; in this case consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer.\n   192\t\n   193\t\\begin{definition}[PCC and SPCC strategies]\\label{def:spcc}\n   194\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy.IsPCC, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC}\n   195\t\t\\leanok\n   196\t\t\\uses{def:projective-strategy-general, def:consistent-strategy, def:comm-strategy, def:symmetric-game}\n   197\t\tWe say that a strategy $\\mathcal S$ for a game $\\mathfrak G$ is \\emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\\mathfrak G$. Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\\mathcal S$ is \\emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.\n   198\t\\end{definition}\n   199\t\n   200\t\\section{Distance measures}\n   201\t\n   202\t\\begin{definition}[Distance between states]\\label{def:state-distance}\n   203\t\tLet $\\{\\ket{\\psi_n}\\}_{n \\in \\N}$ and $\\{\\ket{\\psi'_n}\\}_{n \\in \\N}$ be two families of states in the same space $\\mathcal H$. For a function $\\delta \\colon \\N \\to [0,1]$ we say that $\\{\\ket{\\psi_n}\\}$ and $\\{\\ket{\\psi'_n}\\}$ are \\emph{$\\delta$-close}, denoted $\\ket{\\psi} \\approx_\\delta \\ket{\\psi'}$, if\n   204\t\t\\[\n   205\t\t\t\\lVert \\ket{\\psi_n} - \\ket{\\psi'_n} \\rVert^2 = O(\\delta(n))\\,.\n   206\t\t\\]\n   207\t\tThe dependence of the states and of $\\delta$ on the indexing parameter $n$ is generally left implicit; we write, e.g., $\\ket{\\psi}$ for $\\ket{\\psi_n}$.\n   208\t\\end{definition}\n   209\t\n   210\t\\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]\\label{def:consistency}\n   211\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.consistencyDefect, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentWithin}\n   212\t\t\\leanok\n   213\t\t\\uses{def:povm-conventions, def:state-distance}\n   214\t\tLet $\\mathcal X$ be a finite set and $\\mu$ a distribution on $\\mathcal X$. Let $\\ket{\\psi} \\in \\mathcal H_A \\ot \\mathcal H_B$ be a quantum state, and for all $x \\in \\mathcal X$ let $\\{A^x_a\\}$ and $\\{B^x_a\\}$ be POVMs. We write\n   215\t\t\\[\n   216\t\t\tA^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\simeq_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a\n   217\t\t\\]\n   218\t\ton state $\\ket{\\psi}$ and distribution $\\mu$ if\n   219\t\t\\[\n   220\t\t\t\\E_{x \\sim \\mu} \\sum_{a \\ne b} \\bra{\\psi} A^x_a \\ot B^x_b \\ket{\\psi} = O(\\delta)\\,.\n   221\t\t\\]\n   222\t\tIn this case we say that $\\{A^x_a\\}$ and $\\{B^x_a\\}$ are \\emph{$\\delta$-consistent} on $\\ket{\\psi}$. As in Definition~\\ref{def:state-distance}, the $O(\\cdot)$ refers to families of POVMs and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n \\in \\N$, and is taken as $n \\to \\infty$.\n   223\t\\end{definition}\n   224\t\n   225\tA measurement that is consistent on $\\ket{\\psi}$ in the sense of Definition~\\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same state under the singleton distribution, and vice versa: if $\\sum_a \\bra{\\psi} M_a \\ot M_a \\ket{\\psi} = 1$, then $M_a \\ot \\Id\\, \\ket{\\psi} = \\Id \\ot M_a\\, \\ket{\\psi}$ for every $a$, by the equality case of the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied outcome by outcome.\n   226\t\n   227\t% The source (references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:257-274) states this\n   228\t% definition for pairs of POVMs but applies the relation to arbitrary operator families:\n   229\t% to plain operators at 06:313-330, to sets of matrices at 06:364-380, and to products and\n   230\t% commutators, compared against the zero family, at 06:409-445. The general form below,\n   231\t% for arbitrary finite families of operators, is the one of the NEEXP source\n   232\t% (references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:385-391), from which the distance\n   233\t% calculus is imported; the POVM case is singled out after the display.\n   234\t\\begin{definition}[State-dependent distance between operator families]\\label{def:povm-distance}\n   235\t\t\\uses{def:povm-conventions, def:state-distance}\n   236\t\tLet $\\mathcal X$ and $\\mathcal A$ be finite sets and $\\mu$ a distribution on $\\mathcal X$. Let $\\ket{\\psi} \\in \\mathcal H$ be a quantum state, and for all $x \\in \\mathcal X$ let $\\{M^x_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ and $\\{N^x_a\\}_{a \\in \\mathcal A}$ be two families of linear operators on $\\mathcal H$. We say that \\emph{$\\{M^x_a\\}$ and $\\{N^x_a\\}$ are $\\delta$-close on state $\\ket{\\psi}$ and under distribution $\\mu$} if\n   237\t\t\\[\n   238\t\t\t\\E_{x \\sim \\mu} \\sum_a \\lVert (M^x_a - N^x_a)\\, \\ket{\\psi} \\rVert^2 \\le O(\\delta)\\,,\n   239\t\t\\]\n   240\t\tand we write $M^x_a \\approx_\\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state $\\ket{\\psi}$ and the distribution $\\mu$ are clear from context. This distance is referred to as the \\emph{state-dependent} distance. The principal case is that in which $\\{M^x_a\\}$ and $\\{N^x_a\\}$ are POVMs on $\\mathcal H$, and we then speak of the state-dependent distance between the POVMs; but the relation is used for arbitrary operator families --- for instance for products of measurement operators, or for commutators compared against the identically zero family, as in Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} below.\n   241\t\\end{definition}\n   242\t\n   243\t\\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]\\label{def:strategy-distance}\n   244\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.AreCloseStrategies}\n   245\t\t\\leanok\n   246\t\t\\uses{def:tensor-product-strategy, def:state-distance, def:povm-distance}\n   247\t\tLet $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal Y, \\mathcal A, \\mathcal B, \\mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game and let $\\mathcal S = (\\psi, A, B)$ and $\\mathcal S' = (\\psi', A', B')$ be strategies for $\\mathfrak G$. For $\\delta \\in [0,1]$ we say that \\emph{$\\mathcal S$ is $\\delta$-close to $\\mathcal S'$} if the following conditions hold.\n   248\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   249\t\t\t\\item The states $\\ket{\\psi}, \\ket{\\psi'}$ are states in the same Hilbert space $\\mathcal H_A \\ot \\mathcal H_B$ and are $\\delta$-close.\n   250\t\t\t\\item For all $x \\in \\mathcal X$ and $y \\in \\mathcal Y$, we have $A^x_a \\approx_\\delta (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \\approx_\\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations holding under the distribution $\\mu$ (i.e.\\ under its corresponding marginals), on either $\\ket{\\psi}$ or $\\ket{\\psi'}$.\n   251\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   252\t\\end{definition}\n   253\t\n   254\t\\begin{remark}[Asymptotic reading of the distance relations]\\label{rem:asymptotic-distance}\n   255\t\tDefinitions~\\ref{def:state-distance}, \\ref{def:consistency}, and \\ref{def:povm-distance} are asymptotic: every $\\approx_\\delta$ and $\\simeq_\\delta$ statement refers to families of states and measurement families indexed by an implicit parameter $n \\in \\N$, and the $O(\\cdot)$ is taken as $n \\to \\infty$. None of these relations is a pointwise inequality with an explicit constant. By contrast, the corresponding relations used in the low individual degree chapters (Definitions~\\ref{def:simeq} and~\\ref{def:approx_delta}) carry no hidden constant. Any explicit quantitative version of the present relations therefore retains the constants absorbed into the $O(\\cdot)$; for instance, the triangle inequality of Lemma~\\ref{fact:triangle} carries a factor $2$ inside the $O(\\cdot)$.\n   256\t\\end{remark}\n   257\t\n   258\tWe record several useful facts about the consistency measure and the state-dependent distance. For the statements imported without proof, readers are referred to Sections~4.4 and~4.5 of \\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.\n   259\t\n   260\t\\begin{lemma}[Consistency versus closeness; Fact 4.13 in \\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}]\\label{fact:agreement}\n   261\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.opFamilyDistSq_le_two_mul_consistencyDefect, MIPStarRE.QPBT.consistencyDefect_le_opFamilyDistSq_of_projective}\n   262\t\t\\leanok\n   263\t\t\\uses{def:consistency, def:povm-distance}\n   264\t\tFor POVMs $\\{A^x_a\\}$ and $\\{B^x_a\\}$, the following hold.\n   265\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   266\t\t\t\\item If $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\simeq_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$, then $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\approx_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$.\n   267\t\t\t\\item If $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\approx_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$ \\emph{and} $\\{A^x_a\\}$ and $\\{B^x_a\\}$ are projective measurements, then $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\simeq_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$.\n   268\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   269\t\\end{lemma}\n   270\t\\begin{proof}\n   271\t\t\\leanok\n   272\t\t\\uses{lem:distance-consistency-term,\n   273\t\t\tlem:distance-point-distance-le-defect,\n   274\t\t\tlem:distance-projective-point-distance, lem:distance-nonnegative}\n   275\t\tStated in the source without proof; this is Fact 4.13 of \\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. For the first item, expand each term $\\lVert (A^x_a \\ot \\Id - \\Id \\ot B^x_a)\\ket{\\psi} \\rVert^2$ and use $ (A^x_a)^2 \\le A^x_a$, $(B^x_a)^2 \\le B^x_a$ together with completeness of the two POVMs: summing over $a$ and averaging over $x$ bounds the total by at most twice the off-diagonal mass, which is $O(\\delta)$ by hypothesis. When both families are projective the two operator inequalities hold with equality, so the expansion equals exactly twice the off-diagonal mass; reading this identity in the other direction gives the second item.\n   276\t\\end{proof}\n   277\t\n   278\t\\begin{lemma}[Consistency from closeness with one projective family; Fact 4.14 in \\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}]\\label{fact:agreement-one-sided}\n   279\t\t% Status: the statement is final; no Lean declaration exists yet for the full disjunctive form, so this node carries no formalization marker.\n   280\t\t\\uses{def:consistency, def:povm-distance}\n   281\t\tLet $\\{A^x_a\\}$ and $\\{B^x_a\\}$ be POVMs. If $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\approx_\\delta \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$ and either $\\{A^x_a\\}$ or $\\{B^x_a\\}$ is a projective measurement, then $A^x_a \\ot \\Id_B \\simeq_{\\delta^{1/2}} \\Id_A \\ot B^x_a$.\n   282\t\\end{lemma}\n   283\t\\begin{proof}\n   284\t\t\\uses{lem:distance-projective-left-square-root}\n   285\t\tStated in the source without proof; it is Fact 4.14 of \\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Write the off-diagonal mass $\\sum_{a \\ne b} \\bra{\\psi} A^x_a \\ot B^x_b \\ket{\\psi}$ as an inner product involving $(A^x_a \\ot \\Id - \\Id \\ot B^x_a)\\ket{\\psi}$, using projectivity of one of the two families, and apply the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality; this route costs a square root in the error. Only the branch in which $\\{A^x_a\\}$ is the projective family is available, as Lemma~\\ref{lem:agreement-projective-left}; the branch in which only $\\{B^x_a\\}$ is projective is still open.\n   286\t\\end{proof}\n   287\t\n   288\t\\begin{lemma}[Left-projective branch of Lemma~\\ref{fact:agreement-one-sided}]\\label{lem:agreement-projective-left}\n   289\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.consistencyDefect_le_sqrt_of_projective_left}\n   290\t\t\\leanok\n   291\t\t\\uses{def:consistency, def:povm-distance}\n   292\t\tThis entry states only the branch of Lemma~\\ref{fact:agreement-one-sided} in which the left family is the projective one; it is not the full disjunctive statement of the source. Let $\\mu$ be a probability distribution on $\\mathcal X$, let $\\ket{\\psi}$ be a unit vector, and let $\\{A^x_a\\}$ be a projective measurement for every $x$. State-dependent\n  2531\t\tdistance is unchanged when both finite operator families are reindexed along\n  2532\t\tan equivalence of their outcome sets.\n  2533\t\\end{lemma}\n  2534\t\\begin{proof}\n  2535\t\t\\leanok\n  2536\t\tReindex the finite sum defining the distance.\n  2537\t\\end{proof}\n  2538\t\n  2539\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}]\n  2540\t\t\\label{lem:distance-congr}\n  2541\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_congr}\n  2542\t\t\\leanok\n  2543\t\t\\uses{def:povm-distance}\n  2544\t\tThis formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper; it\n  2545\t\trecords extensionality used in Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}.\n  2546\t\tPointwise equal pairs of operator families have equal state-dependent\n  2547\t\tdistance.\n  2548\t\\end{lemma}\n  2549\t\\begin{proof}\n  2550\t\t\\leanok\n  2551\t\tSubstitute the pointwise equalities in the defining finite sums.\n  2552\t\\end{proof}\n  2553\t\n  2554\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}]\n  2555\t\t\\label{lem:distance-congr-sub}\n  2556\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_congr_sub}\n  2557\t\t\\leanok\n  2558\t\t\\uses{def:povm-distance}\n  2559\t\tThis formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper; it\n  2560\t\trecords the difference form of extensionality used in\n  2561\t\tLemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}. If $A^x_a-B^x_a=A'^x_a-B'^x_a$\n  2562\t\tpointwise, then $d_\\psi(A,B)^2=d_\\psi(A',B')^2$.\n  2563\t\\end{lemma}\n  2564\t\\begin{proof}\n  2565\t\t\\leanok\n  2566\t\tSubstitute the pointwise equality of differences in the defining finite\n  2567\t\tsums.\n  2568\t\\end{proof}\n  2569\t\n  2570\t\\begin{definition}[Formalization support for Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}]\n  2571\t\t\\label{def:distance-swap-last}\n  2572\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.swapLast}\n  2573\t\t\\leanok\n  2574\t\tThis formalization-only definition is not named in the paper; it makes the\n  2575\t\treindexing in Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} explicit. It is the\n  2576\t\tequivalence\n  2577\t\t\\[\n  2578\t\t\t((a,c),b)\\longmapsto((a,b),c)\n  2579\t\t\\]\n  2580\t\tbetween the two associations of the three outcome coordinates.\n  2581\t\\end{definition}\n  2582\t\n  2583\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}]\n  2584\t\t\\label{lem:distance-swap-last-inverse}\n  2585\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.swapLast_symm_apply}\n  2586\t\t\\leanok\n  2587\t\t\\uses{def:distance-swap-last}\n  2588\t\tThis formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper; it\n  2589\t\trecords that the inverse coordinate exchange used in\n  2590\t\tLemma~\\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} sends $((a,b),c)$ to $((a,c),b)$.\n  2591\t\\end{lemma}\n  2592\t\\begin{proof}\n  2593\t\t\\leanok\n  2594\t\tThe coordinate exchange is an involution.\n  2595\t\\end{proof}\n  2596\t\n  2597\t\\section{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}\n  2598\t% Paper subsection label sec:cl kept for cross-reference fidelity.\n  2599\t\\label{sec:cl}\n  2600\t\n  2601\tConditionally linear functions specify the question distributions of the games considered in the following chapters in a form that can be ``introspected''. Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element $x \\in V = \\F^n$ and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially to $x^{V_j}$, where $V_1, V_2, \\dots$ is a sequence of complementary register subspaces such that both the linear map $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$, for $j \\ge 2$, may depend on the values taken by the previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$, $L_2(x^{V_2})$, and so on.\n  2602\t\n  2603\tThroughout this section $V$ denotes the linear space $\\F^n$ for some integer $n \\ge 0$, and all the distinguished subspaces of $V$ are register subspaces (Definition~\\ref{def:register-subspace}). If $V_1, V_2, \\dots, V_\\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, \\ell\\}$, we use the subscript range notation\n  2604\t\\[\n  2605\t\tV_{<k} = \\bigoplus_{j\\,:\\,1 \\le j < k} V_j\\,, \\qquad V_{>k} = \\bigoplus_{j\\,:\\,\\ell \\ge j > k} V_j\\,,\n  2606\t\\]\n  2607\tand $V_{\\le k}$, $V_{\\ge k}$ are understood to be $V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively. For a register subspace $V'$ of $V$, the symbol $x^{V'}$ denotes the projection of $x$ onto $V'$ parallel to the complementary register subspace (Definition~\\ref{def:complementary}). Moreover, if $F \\colon V' \\to V'$ is a function and $x \\in V$, we write $x^F$ for $F(x^{V'})$; for example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is shorthand for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.\n  2608\t\n  2609\t\\begin{definition}[Conditionally linear functions]\\label{def:cl-func}\n  2610\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCondLinearOn, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCondLinear}\\uses{def:register-subspace, def:complementary}\n  2611\t\tLet $V$ be $\\F^n$ for some $n \\ge 0$. For all integers $\\ell \\ge 0$ the collection of \\emph{$\\ell$-level conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \\emph{on $V$}) is defined inductively as follows.\n  2612\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n  2613\t\t\t\\item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the $0$ function on $V$.\n  2614\t\t\t\\item Let $\\ell \\ge 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear functions has been defined. The collection of $\\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form: there exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and, for all $v \\in L_1(V_1)$, an $(\\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\\,v}$ on $V_{>1}$, such that for all $x \\in V$,\n  2615\t\t\t\\[\n  2616\t\t\t\tL(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})\\,.\n  2617\t\t\t\\]\n  2618\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n  2619\t\\end{definition}\n  2620\t\n  2621\tWe abbreviate ``conditionally linear'' as \\emph{CL}. Operationally, an $\\ell$-level CL function first applies $L_1$ to $x^{V_1}$; conditioned on the value $x^{L_1}$ it selects a register subspace $V_2$ and a linear map $L_2$ and applies $L_2$ to $x^{V_2}$; and so on, finally outputting $\\sum_{k=1}^{\\ell} x^{L_k}$. Every $1$-level CL function is linear, and conversely every linear map on $V$ is a $1$-level CL function. Moreover, for every $\\ell \\ge 1$ the collection of $\\ell$-level CL functions contains the collection of $(\\ell-1)$-level CL functions.\n  2622\t\n  2623\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for monotonicity of CL levels]\\label{lem:cl-level-mono}\n  2624\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCondLinearOn.mono_level}\n  2625\t\t\\leanok\n  2626\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2627\t\tThis is the support-relative form of the containment observation following Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func}. Let $S$ be a register subspace of $V$, let $L$ be an $\\ell$-level CL function all of whose factor spaces are contained in $S$, and suppose $\\ell \\le k$. Then $L$ is also a $k$-level CL function all of whose factor spaces are contained in $S$.\n  2628\t\\end{lemma}\n  2629\t\\begin{proof}\n  2630\t\t\\leanok\n  2631\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2632\t\tAdjoin $k-\\ell$ empty factor spaces with zero linear maps before the given representation. Each added linear contribution is zero, so the represented function and its support are unchanged.\n  2633\t\\end{proof}\n  2634\t\n  2635\t% Formalization-support nodes.  The two statements below are not results of the source\n  2636\t% article; the first is the converse half of the observation preceding\n  2637\t% Lemma~\\ref{lem:cl-level-mono}, and the second isolates the transport of a conditionally\n  2638\t% linear function along an injective identification of registers, so that the Lean proofs\n  2639\t% of the question maps of the Pauli basis test remain traceable.\n  2640\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for linear maps as one-level CL functions]\\label{lem:cl-one-level-linear}\n  2641\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear}\n  2642\t\t\\leanok\n  2643\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace}\n  2644\t\tThis is the support-relative form of the converse observation following Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func}. Let $L$ be a linear map on $V$. Then $L$ is a $1$-level CL function all of whose factor spaces are contained in $V$.\n  2645\t\\end{lemma}\n  2646\t\\begin{proof}\n  2647\t\t\\leanok\n  2648\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2649\t\tTake the single factor space $V_1 = V$ with first-level linear map $L_1 = L$, and take the $0$-level function on $V_{>1}$ for every value of $x^{L_1}$. Since $x^V = x$, the represented function sends $x$ to $L(x) + 0 = L(x)$.\n  2650\t\\end{proof}\n  2651\t\n  2652\t\\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for reindexing a CL function]\\label{lem:cl-reindex}\n  2653\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinearOn_reindex}\n  2654\t\t\\leanok\n  2655\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace}\n  2656\t\tThis is not a named statement of the source article; it isolates the transport of a CL function between register spaces used in the Lean proof of the conditional linearity of the Pauli question maps. Let $V' = \\F^{n'}$ and $V = \\F^{n}$, and let $f$ be an injective map of the coordinates of $V'$ into the coordinates of $V$, so that every register subspace of $V'$ is carried to a register subspace of $V$. Let $L$ be an $\\ell$-level CL function on $V'$. Let $\\tilde L \\colon V \\to V$ send $x$ to the vector whose coordinate at $f(k)$ is the $k$-th coordinate of $L\\bigl( (x_{f(k)})_k \\bigr)$ and whose coordinates outside the image of $f$ are zero. Then $\\tilde L$ is an $\\ell$-level CL function on $V$.\n  2657\t\\end{lemma}\n  2658\t\\begin{proof}\n  2659\t\t\\leanok\n  2660\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2661\t\tInduction on $\\ell$. At level $0$ both functions are zero. At level $\\ell \\ge 1$, transport a representation of $L$ term by term: the factor space $V'_1$ is carried to its image under $f$, the first-level linear map $L_1$ to the composition of restriction along $f$ with $L_1$ followed by extension by zero off the image, and the conditional remainders are transported by the induction hypothesis, their prefix values being transported along $f$ as well. Since $f$ is injective, the coordinate at $f(k)$ of a transported vector is the $k$-th coordinate of the vector transported, so the transported representation evaluates to the transport of the value of $L$; outside the image of $f$ both sides vanish.\n  2662\t\\end{proof}\n  2663\t\n  2664\t\\begin{definition}[Conditionally linear distributions]\\label{def:cl-dist}\n  2665\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.clDistribution}\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2666\t\tLet $L, R \\colon V \\to V$ be conditionally linear functions. The \\emph{conditionally linear distribution $\\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,R)$} is the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \\in V \\times V$ for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.\n  2667\t\\end{definition}\n  2668\t\n  2669\tNote that both players' questions are generated from the \\emph{same} uniformly random seed $x$; this shared-seed structure is what the introspection technique exploits. The following lemma elucidates the structural properties of $\\ell$-level CL functions. Recall that $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,\\,u}(x^{V_{k,\\,u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.\n  2670\t\n  2671\t\\begin{lemma}[Structure of conditionally linear functions]\\label{lem:cl-kth}\n  2672\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CLData, MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinear_iff_nonempty_clData}\n  2673\t\t\\leanok\n  2674\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace}\n  2675\t\tLet $\\ell \\ge 1$ and $V = \\F^n$ for some integer $n \\ge 0$. A function $L \\colon V \\to V$ is an $\\ell$-level CL function if and only if the following collection of functions and subspaces exists:\n  2676\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n  2677\t\t\t\\item[(i)] for each $k \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, \\ell\\}$, a function $L_{\\le k} \\colon V \\to V$, called the \\emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};\n  2678\t\t\t\\item[(ii)] for each $k \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, \\ell\\}$ and $u \\in L_{<k}(V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\\,u}$ of $V$, called the \\emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};\n  2679\t\t\t\\item[(iii)] for each $k \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, \\ell\\}$ and $u \\in L_{<k}(V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\\,u} \\colon V_{k,\\,u} \\to V_{k,\\,u}$, called the \\emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};\n  2680\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n  2681\t\tsuch that the following conditions hold for all $k \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, \\ell\\}$:\n  2682\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n  2683\t\t\t\\item $L_{\\le k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;\n  2684\t\t\t\\item $V = \\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\\ell} V_{i,\\,x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \\in V$;\n  2685\t\t\t\\item $L_{\\le k}(x) = \\sum_{i=1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for all $x \\in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\\,x^{L_{<i}}}$;\n  2686\t\t\t\\item $L = L_{\\le \\ell}$.\n  2687\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n  2688\t\tAs in condition 3, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote $V_{k,\\,u}$ and $L_{k,\\,u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.\n  2689\t\tIndex the decomposition levels by $0,\\ldots,\\ell-1$; level $r$ corresponds\n  2690\t\tto the paper's level $r+1$.\n  2691\t\\end{lemma}\n  2692\t\\begin{proof}\n  2693\t\t\\leanok\n  2694\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, lem:cl-restriction-idem}\n  2695\t\tFor the ``if'' direction, conditions 1 and 4 immediately exhibit $L$ as an $\\ell$-level CL function. For the ``only if'' direction one constructs the marginals, factor spaces, and linear maps by induction on $\\ell$. In the base case $\\ell = 1$ take $L_{\\le 1} = L$, $V_1 = V$, and $L_1 = L$. For the inductive step, write $L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func} and apply the inductive hypothesis to each $(\\ell-1)$-level function $L_{>1,\\,v}$, obtaining its marginals, factor spaces, and linear maps over $V_{>1}$. Define $L_{\\le 1} = L_1$ with first factor space $V_1$, and for $k \\ge 2$ define $L_{\\le k}(x) = x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\\,<k}(x^{V_{>1}})$, with the $k$-th factor space and linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$ given by those of $L_{>1,\\,v}$ at index $k-1$ with prefix $w$, where $v = u^{V_1}$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}}$. Conditions 1--4 are then verified directly from the inductive hypothesis: the direct-sum decomposition of $V_{>1}$ extends to $V$ by adjoining $V_1$, and the sum formula for $L_{\\le k}$ follows by unfolding the inductive marginals.\n  2696\t\\end{proof}\n  2697\t\n  2698\tThe marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given CL function $L$ need not be unique. For example, the identity function on $V = \\F^n$ is a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a $k$-level CL function for any $k \\in \\{2, \\dots, n\\}$ with an arbitrary partition of $V$ into factor spaces.\n  2699\t\n  2700\t\\begin{lemma}[Concatenation of conditionally linear functions]\\label{lem:cl-concat}\n  2701\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCondLinearOn.concat}\n  2702\t\t\\leanok\n  2703\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2704\t\tLet $\\ell, k \\ge 0$ be integers and let $U = \\F^n$, $V = \\F^m$ be linear spaces. Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and, for each $u \\in L(U)$, $R_u$ is an $\\ell$-level CL function on $V$. Then the \\emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\\{R_u\\}_u$, defined by\n  2705\t\t\\[\n  2706\t\t\tT(x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)}(x^V)\\,,\n  2707\t\t\\]\n  2708\t\tis a $(k+\\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U \\oplus V$.\n  2709\t\\end{lemma}\n  2710\t\\begin{proof}\n  2711\t\t\\leanok\n  2712\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func}\n  2713\t\tBy induction on $k$. The case $k = 0$ follows directly from Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func}, since then $L = 0$ and $T$ acts by the single $\\ell$-level function $R_0$ on the register subspace $V$. For the inductive step, write $L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}})$ with complementary register subspaces $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$. For each value $x^{L_1}$, the function $T_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \\oplus V$ sending $x^{U_{>1} \\oplus V}$ to $L_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) + R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V)$ is the concatenation of the $(k-1)$-level function $L_{>1,\\,x^{L_1}}$ with a family drawn from $\\{R_u\\}$, hence is $(k+\\ell-1)$-level by the induction hypothesis. The claim then follows from Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func} applied with first subspace $U_1$ and first linear map $L_1$.\n  2714\t\\end{proof}\n  2715\t\n  2716\t% The source (references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364) leaves\n  2717\t% the number m of summands unquantified (m >= 1 is needed for the level max_j ell_j to\n  2718\t% have an index) and begins its induction at level 1; the level-zero base case is supplied\n  2719\t% here, since def:cl-func admits 0-level functions and all ell_j may be 0.\n  2720\t\\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of conditionally linear functions]\\label{lem:cl-func-prod}\n  2721\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCondLinear.directSum}\n  2722\t\t\\leanok\n  2723\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace}\n  2724\t\tLet $m \\ge 1$ be an integer and let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \\dots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that $V = \\bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$. Suppose that, for each $j \\in \\{1, 2, \\dots, m\\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an $\\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$. Then the direct sum $L = \\bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$, defined by\n  2725\t\t\\[\n  2726\t\t\tL(x) = \\sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})\n  2727\t\t\\]\n  2728\t\tfor all $x = \\sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \\in \\bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$, is an $\\ell$-level CL function on $V$ for $\\ell = \\max_j \\{\\ell_j\\}$; the maximum exists since $m \\ge 1$.\n  2729\t\tWith zero-based indices, the summand labelled $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,m-1\\}$\n  2730\t\tcorresponds to the paper's summand $j=r+1$.\n  2731\t\\end{lemma}\n  2732\t\\begin{proof}\n  2733\t\t\\leanok\n  2734\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, lem:cl-func-prod-same-level}\n  2735\t\tSince an $\\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level conditionally linear for all $k \\ge \\ell$, it suffices to prove the claim when $\\ell_j = \\ell$ for all $j$. Proceed by induction on $\\ell$. For $\\ell = 0$ every $L^{(j)}$ is the zero function on $V^{(j)}$, so $L$ is the zero function on $V$, which is the unique $0$-level CL function on $V$ (Definition~\\ref{def:cl-func}). For the inductive step with $\\ell \\ge 1$, decompose each $L^{(j)}$ into its first-level linear part $L^{(j)}_1$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and its family of $(\\ell-1)$-level remainders $L^{(j)}_{>1,\\,v_j}$ on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$. The direct sums of the first-level parts define a linear map on $V_1 = \\bigoplus_j V^{(j)}_1$, and, for each prefix value $v = \\sum_j v_j$, the direct sums of the remainders are $(\\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear on $V_{>1} = \\bigoplus_j V^{(j)}_{>1}$ by the induction hypothesis. +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_32","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,110p' MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Sandwich/Defs.lean\"","aggregated_output":"import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs\nimport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems\nimport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.ErrorFunctions\n\n/-! # Definitions for sandwiched measurements\n\nThis module defines the palindromic operator products and the conditional\ncollision predicate used by the sandwich and pasting lemmas.\n\n## References\n\nBlueprint `lem:ld-sandwich` and `lem:pasting`; paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-525`.\n-/\n\nopen scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder\n\nnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n\nopen MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement\nopen MIPStarRE.Quantum\nopen DistanceCalculus\n\nnamespace SandwichProduct\n\n/-- The ordered product of coordinate effects, defined recursively by placing\nthe final coordinate effect on both sides of the preceding product. This is the\npalindromic product in `lem:ld-sandwich`; blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/\nnoncomputable def orderedCoordinateProduct {ι : Type*}\n    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :\n    (k : ℕ) → (Γ : Fin k → Type*) →\n      ((i : Fin k) → Γ i → Op ι) → ((i : Fin k) → Γ i) → Op ι\n  | 0, _, _, _ => 1\n  | 1, _, G, g => G 0 (g 0)\n  | k + 2, Γ, G, g =>\n      G (Fin.last (k + 1)) (g (Fin.last (k + 1))) *\n        orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)\n          (fun i a => G i.castSucc a) (fun i => g i.castSucc) *\n        G (Fin.last (k + 1)) (g (Fin.last (k + 1)))\n\nend SandwichProduct\n\n/-- The ordered product\n`G^k_{g_k} ... G^1_{g_1} ... G^k_{g_k}` of `lem:ld-sandwich`.\n\n**Local fix:** The source reverses the outcome indices, so the printed\nexpression is undefined when the outcome families differ. This definition uses\nthe pairing corrected in\n`rem:ld-sandwich-indexing` and\n`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-sandwich-indexing.tex`; blueprint statement\n`lem:ld-sandwich` and remark `rem:ld-sandwich-indexing`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. Tracked in\nissue #16. The empty product is `1`. -/\nnoncomputable def sandwichProduct {k : ℕ} {X ι : Type*}\n    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {Γ : Fin k → Type*}\n    (G : (i : Fin k) → X → Γ i → Op ι) (x : X)\n    (g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i) : Op ι :=\n  SandwichProduct.orderedCoordinateProduct k Γ (fun i a => G i x a) g\n\n/-- The two-family sandwiched product\n`(G₂)_{g₂} (G₁)_{g₁} (G₂)_{g₂}` from blueprint\n`eq:pasting-2a`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. -/\ndef pastedMeasurement {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n    {G₁ G₂ : Type*} (M₁ : G₁ → Op ι) (M₂ : G₂ → Op ι)\n    (g₁ : G₁) (g₂ : G₂) : Op ι :=\n  M₂ g₂ * M₁ g₁ * M₂ g₂\n\n/-- Evaluating a tuple of codewords at a common point. This is a\nformalization-only auxiliary for blueprint\n`lem:ld-sandwich`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-495`. -/\ndef evalFunctionTuple {k : ℕ} {Y : Type*} {R Γ : Fin k → Type*}\n    (eval : (i : Fin k) → Γ i → Y → R i) (y : Y)\n    (g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i) : (i : Fin k) → R i :=\n  fun i => eval i (g i) y\n\n/-- The positive-mass conditional collision bound used by `lem:pasting`.\nThis is a formalization-only spelling of the conditional probability in\n`lem:pasting`, with paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. -/\ndef HasConditionalCollisionBound {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}\n    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]\n    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]\n    [Fintype Γ₂]\n    (D : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂)) (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂)\n    (η : ℝ) : Prop :=\n  ∀ x y₁, 0 < (D.map Prod.fst).weight (x, y₁) →\n    ∀ g g' : Γ₂, g ≠ g' →\n      (∑ y₂ : Y₂, D.weight ((x, y₁), y₂) *\n        if eval₂ g y₂ = eval₂ g' y₂ then 1 else 0) ≤\n        η * (D.map Prod.fst).weight (x, y₁)\n\n\n/-! ### Tensor placements of measurements\n\nThe operator families compared in `lem:pasting` are placed on one factor of a\nbipartite space. Formalization support for `lem:pasting`, blueprint\n`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:960-990`. -/\nnoncomputable def Measurement.leftPlacement {α ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype α]\n    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]\n    (M : Measurement α ιA) : Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=\n  DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement M\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The correction is documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_polynomial-error-square-root.tex` and tracked by issue\n#16. -/\ndef IsPolyErr (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=\n  ∃ C r : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ 0 < r ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ x →\n    0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ C * Real.rpow x r\n\n/-- A nonnegative two-parameter error function bounded by a sum of positive\nreal powers.\n\n**Local fix:** The prefactor and the two exponents are quantified separately,\nand the bound is imposed on the closed nonnegative quadrant. Tracked in \\ghissue{201}.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\section{Key theorem forms}\n\nThe source asks for an error function\n$\\delta_{\\mathrm{pasting}}(\\eta,\\delta)$ satisfying\n\\[\n  \\delta_{\\mathrm{pasting}}(\\eta,\\delta)\n    = \\operatorname{poly}(\\eta,\\delta)\n\\]\nand bounding the final consistency defect whenever the three input defects are\nat most $\\delta$ and the codeword-collision probability is at most $\\eta$.\nUnder the paper's global convention, the displayed polynomial assertion means\nthat there is a universal $C>0$ such that\n\\[\n  0 \\leq \\delta_{\\mathrm{pasting}}(\\eta,\\delta)\n    \\leq C(\\eta\\delta)^C\n  \\qquad (\\eta,\\delta>0).\n  \\tag{product contract}\n\\]\nThe imported proof instead accumulates terms depending separately on the two\nerrors, including $O(\\delta^{1/2})$, $O((\\delta+\\eta)^{1/2})$, and $\\eta$.\nA compatible corrected theorem form would use, for example, an upper bound by\n$A(\\eta^r+\\delta^s)$ for universal $A\\geq1$ and $r,s>0$.\n\n\\section{The source assertion}\n\nLemma~\\texttt{lem:pasting} of \\cite[lines~504--525]{Ji2020MIPStar} imports\nFact~4.35 from the NEEXP paper. The proof of the imported\nfact, however, bounds the two sources of error independently; see\n\\cite[lines~1030--1209]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.%\n\\footnote{The mirrored passages are\n\\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}, lines~19--29;\n\\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~504--525;\nand \\path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex},\nlines~1030--1209.}\n\nMore explicitly, fix a probability distribution $\\mathcal D$ on\n$(x,y_1,y_2)$, a unit bipartite state $\\psi$, and nonnegative $\\eta,\\delta$.\nLet $G_i^x$ be measurements indexed by functions\n$g_i:\\mathcal Y_i\\to\\mathcal R_i$, with $G_2^x$ projective, and let\n$A^{x,y_1,y_2}$ be a projective joint answer measurement. In the\nstandard basis, take the normalized bipartite state\n\\[\n  \\ket{\\psi_\\rho}\n    = \\sqrt{1-\\rho}\\ket{0,0}+\\sqrt{\\rho}\\ket{1,1}.\n\\]\nLet both codeword measurements have their sole effect equal to the identity,\nand evaluate the sole first codeword to $0$.  Let the joint answer measurement\nbe the standard-basis projective measurement: its effects at $(0,*)$ and\n$(1,*)$ are respectively $\\ket{0}\\!\\bra{0}$ and $\\ket{1}\\!\\bra{1}$.\n\nThe second codeword set is a singleton, so its pairwise-collision hypothesis is\nvacuous for every $\\eta\\geq0$.
